kurz: Which figures and disclosures in the annual report reveal a company's problems before they show up in the share price.

bloecke.md:
Genuine accounting fraud is rare; aggressive accounting, on the other hand, is common. In between lies a broad grey area in which figures are legally presented so that they look better than the business they depict. Investors in individual shares do not need forensic auditing expertise for this. A handful of figures that show when presentation and business diverge is enough.

At Enron, Steinhoff and Wirecard, the signals were not hidden. They were in published financial statements, namely in the notes, in the cash flow statement and in the development of receivables. They were simply ignored because revenue was rising.

Reported profit depends on accounting decisions; cash flow is based on verifiable payments. Almost every serious warning sign can be traced back to reported profit and cash flow diverging over years, with the difference building up in balance sheet items instead of unwinding again.

## Revenue growth without rising cash flow (signal 1)

Revenue is booked as soon as it is realised, regardless of when payment is made. Between net profit and operating cash flow therefore lie the accruals, that is changes in receivables, inventories, provisions and capitalised costs. In an unremarkable year they roughly balance out. Because depreciation reduces profit without costing money, operating cash flow is normally above net profit.

If it is persistently below net profit, that is an exceptional situation. Two ratios are enough to measure the deviation.

bloecke.formel:
Cash conversion = operating cash flow / net profit
Accrual ratio = (net profit − operating cash flow) / balance sheet total
bloecke.erklaerung: Over a full cycle, cash conversion should average 1 or more. The accrual ratio relates the gap to the size of the company and is therefore comparable over years and between companies. Both figures should be looked at cumulatively over five years. For a single year they say little, because working capital fluctuates seasonally.
variablen: cash inflow from operating activities, cash flow statement
profit after tax from the income statement
better: average of the opening and closing figures for the year

bloecke.titel: Revenue, receivables and operating cash flow (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: Fictitious company, indexed to 2021 = 100; revenue doubles, receivables triple and operating cash flow falls sharply.

bloecke.md:
The most important figure is in the last row. Over five years, €326 million of profit was reported and €160 million of cash came in. Half of the profit therefore exists only as balance sheet items. A single weak year would say little; five years of continuously falling cash conversion, by contrast, form a pattern.

Where the money went is shown line by line in the indirect cash flow statement.

bloecke.titel: From profit to cash flow, financial year 2025 (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: Depreciation increases cash flow, but the build-up of receivables and inventories exceeds the entire net profit.

bloecke.md:
## Disproportionately growing receivables and inventories (signal 2)

Days sales outstanding converts the level of receivables into days and so makes it comparable over years. If it rises without any recognisable change in the business model, there are three possible explanations. Customers are paying less reliably, the company is winning revenue through longer payment terms, or part of the revenue is booked before it has been earned. All three are bad; the third is the most serious.

bloecke.formel:
DSO = average trade receivables / revenue × 365
DIO = average inventories / cost of sales × 365
Cash conversion cycle = DIO + DSO − DPO
bloecke.erklaerung: When an HGB (Commercial Code) income statement uses the nature of expense method, cost of sales does not appear in it. The cost of materials serves as an approximation, which should be disclosed when making comparisons. A negative cycle means that the customer pays before the company pays its suppliers. In food retail and subscription models this is normal; elsewhere it needs explaining. For simplicity, the illustrative calculation in this lesson uses receivables at year-end. With average values, DSO for 2025 would be around 84 instead of 99 days.

bloecke.titel: Days sales outstanding in the illustrative calculation
bloecke.unter: Calculated using receivables at year-end. Days sales outstanding rises from 60 to 99 days, so that by the end a full quarter's revenue is tied up in unpaid invoices and is not in the bank account.

bloecke.md:
## Aggressive capitalisation (signal 3)

If an expenditure is capitalised, that is recorded in the balance sheet as an asset instead of being booked as an expense, the burden shifts into the future. Profit and equity rise in the current year, and the amortisation weighs on later years. Under IAS 38, research costs are always expensed immediately, while development costs must be capitalised if the criteria of the standard are met. The HGB, by contrast, grants a capitalisation option for self-created intangible assets in Section 248(2) sentence 1. Self-created brands, customer lists and publishing rights may not be capitalised under either the HGB or IAS 38.

A side effect is more important. Capitalisation also increases operating cash flow, because the payment then appears in investing cash flow. In this way a company can improve profit and operating cash flow at the same time without more money coming in.

Besides capitalisation, factoring shortly before the reporting date, stretched supplier payments and reverse factoring also increase reported operating cash flow without anything having changed in the business. As a cross-check, look at free cash flow after capital expenditure, read the item *own work capitalised* and capital expenditure (capex) as well, and check whether trade payables rise conspicuously in the fourth quarter.

## People and auditors (signal 4)

Today, a change of auditor is not a warning sign in itself, because mandatory rotation provides for regular changes. What stands out is the pattern and the timing, for example a change outside the regular rotation shortly before the audit of a contentious matter, or several chief financial officers within a few years. At Enron, Steinhoff and Wirecard there were no such changes. Arthur Andersen, Deloitte and EY remained auditors until the collapse, and there was no cluster of changes of chief financial officer either. What did stand out at Enron and Wirecard was the aggressive public reaction to critics and short sellers.

The notes contain two relevant disclosures. The auditor's fees are broken down into audit and other services (Section 285 no. 17 HGB), and transactions with related companies and persons are disclosed (Section 285 no. 21 HGB).

In 2000, Arthur Andersen received around $25 million in audit fees from Enron and around a further $27 million for consulting, that is more for consulting than for the audit. The case is regarded as a textbook example of an independence conflict and is one of the reasons why audit fees must now be broken down in the notes. As a rule of thumb, if non-audit services persistently exceed audit services, the auditor's independence can no longer be taken for granted.

## Structure and notes (signal 5)

Fraud needs counterparties that do not object. Enron created them with special purpose vehicles into which losses and debts were shifted. Steinhoff used companies that appeared to be independent third parties but were related and controlled. Wirecard relied on a third-party partner business in Asia whose revenue and balances could hardly be audited.

Three structural features should therefore always be checked. The first is the list of shareholdings in the notes (how many companies, in which jurisdictions, how many of them not consolidated). The second is where earnings come from by segment. Because IFRS 8 follows the management approach, the definition of segments can be changed at any time, and a change of segments is a well-known way of concealing losses. The third is growth that comes mainly from acquisitions and accumulates as [[Goodwill|goodwill]] on the balance sheet. The stress test here is the calculation equity minus goodwill.

bloecke.titel: Three accounting scandals and their consequences
bloecke.unter: In all three cases, the signals were in published documents years before the collapse.

ereignisse.text: The corrections of October and 8 November reduce profits for 1997-2000 by $591 million, increase liabilities by $628 million and reduce equity by $1.2 billion. The Chapter 11 filing follows on 2 December (balance sheet total $63.4 billion).
As a direct consequence, the act lays down the personal responsibility of the CEO and CFO for the financial statements, requires internal control systems and restricts consulting by the auditor.

The CEO resigns on 5 December, and the share loses almost 90% within two weeks. The forensic investigation by PwC identifies around €6.5 billion of fictitious or irregular income between 2009 and 2017.

Trustee account balances of €1.9 billion, around a quarter of the balance sheet total, do not exist. The auditor refuses to issue its audit opinion on 18 June, and the insolvency filing follows on 25 June.

For financial years from 1 January 2027, mandatory subtotals apply in the income statement, together with systematic disclosure requirements for self-defined performance measures for the first time. This improves the comparability of adjusted figures but does not make them more reliable.

bloecke.md:
A growing part of the group's assets was held as trustee account balances with third-party partners instead of as bank balances within the group. In the end it amounted to €1.9 billion, around a quarter of the balance sheet total. At the same time, a large part of reported earnings came from a foreign business that the group did not handle itself. The questions of where the money physically is and who sees the payment flows directly could be asked without inside knowledge.

The KPMG special report of late April 2020 could neither confirm nor refute the existence of the revenue for this third-party partner business. With a quarter of the balance sheet affected, an investor should treat this finding as a result and not as an open question.

Wirecard received unqualified audit opinions for years. An audit opinion under Section 322 HGB certifies reasonable assurance in accordance with auditing standards. It does not confirm that there is no fraud, because the audit is based on samples and materiality. The responsibility statement (Bilanzeid), the assurance given by the legal representatives under Section 264(2) sentence 3 HGB, is likewise a declaration and not proof. It establishes liability but provides no certainty.

bloecke.erklaerung: The Beneish M-score combines eight indices into a single screening value. From −1.78 upwards, a company is considered conspicuous. By far the largest coefficient belongs to TATA, total accruals relative to the balance sheet total. This is the same quantity as the accrual ratio above. The score provides an indication and not proof; its hit rate is below 100%, and it cannot be applied to financial institutions.
variablen: days' sales in receivables index compared with the previous year
gross margin index (a falling margin raises the score)
asset quality: share of assets that are hard to value
index of selling, general and administrative expenses
total accruals divided by balance sheet total

bloecke.md:
## False alarms and harmless explanations

Each of these signals can have harmless causes. Anyone who applies them mechanically will therefore also sell good companies. Negative working capital is a mark of quality in food retail, but a reason for scrutiny in plant engineering. Rising inventories before a product launch serve as preparation and are not a sign of goods failing to sell. A change of auditor may simply follow mandatory rotation. From 2019, IFRS 16 causes a break in time series and raises EBITDA, balance sheet total, net debt and operating cash flow purely through accounting.

A single signal says little. What is informative is the accumulation of signals, their direction over several years and whether the company explains them of its own accord. Good reports name their own inconsistencies; bad ones explain them only when asked.

schritte.titel: Put ten years side by side
schritte.text: Record revenue, net profit, operating cash flow, free cash flow, receivables, inventories, balance sheet total and share count on one sheet, with one row per figure. Trends only become visible over time.

schritte.titel: Measure the gap between profit and cash flow
schritte.text: Compare cumulative net profit with cumulative operating cash flow and calculate the accrual ratio for each year. If it rises steadily, all further checks are mandatory.
Calculate DSO, DIO and DPO over ten years. The direction, and whether it follows the industry trend or runs counter to it, says more than the level.
Work back from the adjusted figure to the IFRS figure. Check whether the same items are adjusted every year and whether income has ever been stripped out.

Go through guarantees and similar commitments, contingent liabilities, related parties, remaining maturities of debt, impairment test assumptions and auditor fees. The notes contain what is missing from the primary statements.

Establish how often and when the CFO and auditor have changed in ten years, how the company responds publicly to criticism and whether the audit opinion contains qualifications or emphasis-of-matter paragraphs.
If the structure cannot be explained in three sentences after this round, that is already a result and not a reason for further research. Passing on the share costs at most a missed opportunity.

bloecke.md: Financial statements of German corporations that are subject to disclosure are published under Section 325 HGB in the Company Register (Unternehmensregister) or the Federal Gazette (Bundesanzeiger). There they can be accessed free of charge and are often more informative than the elaborately designed version on the investor relations website, because the notes and management report are included in full. The management report under Section 289 HGB, with its forecast, opportunities and risk report, is the only mandatory forward-looking information. The auditor assesses it but does not guarantee its content. For US shares, the route is via the SEC's EDGAR database to the 10-K and 8-K reports.

Forged balance confirmations cannot be detected with ratios. At Wirecard, the documents themselves were false, and no ratio calculation helps against that. Only a plausibility check can help. It has to establish whether the margin and the capital tied up fit the claimed business and who other than the company can confirm this. If that remains unclear, not buying is the only reliable protection. Diversification limits the damage but does not prevent it.

mitnehmen: The most reliable early indicator is the gap between cumulative profit and cumulative operating cash flow over five to ten years.
Receivables and inventories should be expressed in days, because rising DSO without a change in the business model is one of the strongest signals of aggressive revenue recognition.
Capitalisation shifts expense into the future and at the same time lifts profit and operating cash flow, so capex and own work capitalised should always be read as well.
An unqualified audit opinion certifies reasonable assurance and does not rule out fraud; the disclosures that matter for risk are in the notes.
A single signal says little; what is informative is an accumulation of signals, their direction over years and evasive explanations from the company.

begriffe.text: The difference between net profit and operating cash flow (Abgrenzungen) that is tied up in receivables, inventories, provisions and capitalised costs. Relative to the balance sheet total it gives the accrual ratio, an early indicator of aggressive accounting.
Operating cash flow divided by net profit. Over a full cycle the figure should be 1 or above, because depreciation reduces profit without costing money.

Days sales outstanding (Debitorenlaufzeit), calculated as average trade receivables divided by revenue times 365. If it rises without a change in the business model, this points to customers' payment problems or premature revenue recognition.

The auditor's opinion (Bestätigungsvermerk) under Section 322 HGB on the financial statements and management report. It certifies reasonable assurance based on sample testing and does not rule out fraud. Qualifications and emphasis-of-matter paragraphs in the opinion are warning signs in their own right.

Screening model made up of eight ratio indices that provides indications of earnings manipulation. Values above −1.78 are considered conspicuous. The model provides no proof, is not error-free and cannot be applied to financial institutions.
